📝Lasers as part of defense📝

Adaptation to growing UAV threats, though slower than desired, is happening and already bearing fruit. Weapons that just a few years ago were perceived in the mass consciousness as an expensive toy and an element of science fiction films are gradually being mastered and becoming a working tool of Russia's air defense.

🖍According to footage from a report on the operation of a next-generation combat laser system, Russian forces have deployed a laser installation capable of striking high-speed air targets. The system is already being successfully used to protect facilities in the southwest of the country. According to the developers, the count of destroyed UAVs runs into the hundreds, and the system is being continuously improved.

🚩However, one should not overestimate this type of weapon — it is far from a panacea. Lasers will not replace air defense systems and will not shoot down UAVs "in batches" on their own. But as part of a comprehensive approach with traditional air defense means, they can significantly strengthen the country's protection against air threats.

📌The cost of a single laser shot is much lower than the cost of launching an air defense missile. And when it comes to mass attacks by cheap UAVs, this becomes a significant factor.

❗️UAV development followed a similar path: from bulky experimental models to compact designs for specific tasks. The same will happen with lasers. The process is underway, the technology is being mastered, and for Russian conditions it is important not to lose this pace. Only real combat experience will show the strengths and weaknesses of this technology.
